newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares inch up, seen rising on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares inch up, seen rising on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares inched up in slightly higher turnover on Friday and analysts said they were likely to rise on Monday on the back of strong buying after price fixing.

But they said they saw the market flat or slightly falling next week as mass privatisation NFI units, which jumped six percent this week in soaring turnovers and 74.7 percent since late August, were drawing investors' interest from stocks.

"I don't see any chance of a rise and a challenging of the (September 18, 14,832.7-point) main-market high soon, as investors apparently have moved their attention to the NFI market," said Tomasz Berent of IB Austria Securities.
NFI units rose 4.8 percent on Friday to a record high of 152 zlotys ($54.2)in the regular bourse session and rose 0.7 percent to 153 zlotys ($54.6) in continuous trade.
NFI turnovers in the continuous and regular sessions together amounted to an all-time high of 104.8 million zlotys ($37.4 million).

The main market's WIG index rose 44.2 points, or 0.3 percent, to 14,675.9, and turnover rose 5.4 percent to 106.7 million zlotys ($38.1 million) on both markets as 45 issues rose, 21 fell and 12 were flat.
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.3 million zlotys ($0.5 million) with biggest mover steel trader Stalexport rising 1.6 percent.
